questions.question: What are the two grammatical consequences of a noun being Ghayr Munsarif?
options: It rejects Tanwin and Damma, accepting only Fatha
It rejects all three harakaat and requires a Huruf al-Jarr in all contexts
It rejects Kasra and Tanwin — Fatha substitutes in the jarr position and Tanwin is dropped entirely
It rejects Damma and Fatha, accepting only Kasra
questions.explanation: Ghayr Munsarif rejects Kasra (replaced by Fatha in the jarr position) and Tanwin (dropped entirely in all positions).

questions.question: What is the key difference between Adl Tahqiqi and Adl Taqdiri?
options: Adl Tahqiqi always pairs with Wasf; Adl Taqdiri always pairs with 'Alamiyya
Adl Tahqiqi is deviation proven by evidence in meaning; Adl Taqdiri is deviation assumed by grammarians without external proof
Adl Tahqiqi applies to proper nouns while Adl Taqdiri applies only to descriptors
Adl Tahqiqi changes a word's meaning; Adl Taqdiri changes only its vowel pattern
questions.explanation: Adl Tahqiqi is verified deviation — there is evidence pointing to the original form, as with ثُلَاث whose repetition in meaning proves the original. Adl Taqdiri is assumed deviation — grammarians inferred the original form with no external evidence, as with عُمَر.

questions.question: What are the two asbab that make ثُلَاث / مَثْلَث Ghayr Munsarif?
options: Wazn Fi'l and Wasf
Wasf and Adl Tahqiqi
'Alamiyya and Wasf
Adl Taqdiri and Ta'nith
questions.explanation: ثُلَاث / مَثْلَث carries Wasf (designed as a descriptor meaning 'three and three') and Adl Tahqiqi (deviated from the original form سَلَاسَةٌ سَلَاسَةٌ, proven by the repetition in its meaning).

questions.question: What is the defining difference between Wasf Asli and Wasf Ardi?
options: Wasf Asli requires Ta'nith to function as a sabab; Wasf Ardi does not
Wasf Asli is found in Ajami words; Wasf Ardi is found in Arabic words
Wasf Asli is born with the word and retained permanently; Wasf Ardi only exists within a specific syntactic structure
Wasf Asli applies only to color adjectives; Wasf Ardi applies to all other adjectives
questions.explanation: Wasf Asli is a quality the word was designed with from the outset and retains permanently regardless of how it is later used. Wasf Ardi is a descriptor function a word only has within a specific syntactic structure — e.g., أَرْبَع as a Sifa for Niswah in that sentence, but not standalone.

questions.question: With which sabab can Adl never pair as the second cause for Ghayr Munsarif?
options: Ta'nith
Wasf
Wazn Fi'l
'Alamiyya
questions.explanation: Adl cannot pair with Wazn Fi'l as its second sabab. Adl commonly pairs with 'Alamiyya (e.g., عُمَر، زُفَر) and with Wasf (e.g., ثُلَاث، مَثْلَث).

questions.question: Why is هِنْد valid as both Munsarif and Ghayr Munsarif?
options: Because it has Ta'nith Ma'nawi and 'Alam, but its middle letter is Sakin al-Awsat and it is Arabic origin, weakening the second sabab
Because it is a foreign-origin word, making its 'Alam status ambiguous
Because Thulathi words with Ta'nith Lafzi are always permitted both rulings by consensus
Because grammarians applied Adl Taqdiri to it, creating two valid interpretations
questions.explanation: هِنْد is Thulathi with Ta'nith Ma'nawi and 'Alam — two asbab in principle — but its middle letter carries sukoon (Sakin al-Awsat) and it is Arabic origin; both sub-conditions failing means the second sabab is weakened, so grammarians accepted both rulings as valid.

questions.question: What does it mean for a noun to be مُنْصَرِف?
options: It accepts all three harakaat and Tanwin — it 'turns' freely through all states of declension
It rejects Tanwin in all positions
It takes Fatha in the jarr position instead of Kasra
It can only occur as the subject of a sentence, never in the jarr position
questions.explanation: Munsarif accepts all three harakaat (Damma, Fatha, Kasra) along with Tanwin; it 'turns' to all states of declension.

questions.question: In the jarr position, what does غَيْر مُنْصَرِف take instead of Kasra?
options: Fatha
Sukoon
Damma
Tanwin al-Fath
questions.explanation: Ghayr Munsarif takes Fatha in the jarr position instead of the expected Kasra.

questions.question: As a sabab for Ghayr Munsarif, what does عَدْل refer to?
options: A grammatical assumption grammarians make when no direct evidence exists
The addition of a Ta' Marbuta to make a word feminine
Deviation from the word's original pattern (Sigha Asliyya) to a different pattern
A shift in the word's meaning from concrete to abstract
questions.explanation: Adl involves a departure from the word's original pattern (Sigha Asliyya) to a different pattern.

questions.question: What does تَقْدِير mean, and how does it apply to عُمَر?
options: Grammatical assumption; grammarians inferred عُمَر's original form was عَامِر to supply a missing second sabab
Literal deviation; grammarians found explicit evidence that عُمَر originally ended in Ta' Marbuta
Phonetic transformation; عُمَر lost its Ta' Marbuta to become Ghayr Munsarif
Semantic inversion; عُمَر's meaning shifted, granting it the quality of Adl
questions.explanation: Taqdir means grammatical assumption — inferring something not explicitly stated. For عُمَر, grammarians assumed the original form was عَامِر to supply the missing second sabab, since only Alamiyya was visibly present.

questions.question: What is the rule regarding وَصْف أَصْلِي once a word possesses it?
options: It applies only while the word is being used in a comparative construction
It is retained permanently — 'once Wasf, forever Wasf' — even if the word shifts in daily use to function as a noun
It is lost when the word enters a genitive structure
It disappears once the word is used more than half the time as a noun
questions.explanation: Wasf Asliyya is never removed — a word designed from the outset to describe retains that quality permanently, even if it later functions primarily as a noun (e.g., أَسْوَد as a name for a type of snake).

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three visible markers of تَأْنِيث لَفْظِي?
options: Shadda on the final letter
Alif mamdūdah (اء)
Nun of the feminine plural (نَّ)
Waw of plural (و)
questions.explanation: The three markers of Ta'nith Lafzi are Tā' marbūṭah (ة), Alif maqṣūrah (ى), and Alif mamdūdah (اء).

questions.question: A Thulāthī word with سَاكِن الأَوْسَط and Arabic origin falls into which category for Ghayr Munsarif purposes?
options: Always Munsarif because Arabic origin overrides the Ta'nith
Both Munsarif and Ghayr Munsarif are valid
Always Ghayr Munsarif because the middle weakness outweighs its Arabic origin
Ghayr Munsarif only if it also carries 'Alamiyya
questions.explanation: With Arabic origin and Sakin al-Awsat, both Munsarif and Ghayr Munsarif are valid — the word sits on the fence, and grammarians accepted both rulings.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between عَلَمِيَّة and وَصْف as the two asbab for Ghayr Munsarif?
options: They can pair together, but only for Thulathi words with Sakin al-Awsat
They commonly pair together when the word is of Ajami origin
They are mutually exclusive — they can never co-occur as the two asbab
They can pair together only when the word also has Ta'nith Ma'nawi
questions.explanation: 'Alamiyya and Wasf are mutually exclusive as the two asbab — they can never co-occur as the pair that triggers Ghayr Munsarif.

questions.question: In the ayah on Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah, which two foundational acts establish Allah's exclusive right to worship?
options: Creating the angels and commanding them to serve the people of faith
Forgiving sins and answering the prayers of the believers
Bringing creation out of non-existence and abundantly bestowing blessings such as rain and sustenance
Sending prophets and revealing scriptures to guide humanity
questions.explanation: Allah alone creates and sustains — bringing creation out of non-existence and bestowing blessings like rain producing crops and fruits. Because He alone does this, He alone deserves worship.

questions.question: In Ayah al-Tahhaddi, who is included in the challenge, and what are they challenged to produce?
options: The Arabs alone; they are challenged to produce ten surahs like the Quran
All of humanity, jinn, and even the idols and false gods; they are challenged to produce a single surah comparable to the Quran
The poets of Arabia; they are challenged to produce a verse surpassing the Quran in meter
The People of the Book; they are challenged to show a scripture older than the Quran
questions.explanation: The challenge is directed at all of humanity, jinn, and the idols/false gods. They fail to produce even a single surah comparable to the Quran in rhetoric, clarity, composition, words, meanings, and legislation.

questions.question: What does لَن communicate in وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا, and how does it differ from لَا?
options: لَن is a question particle introducing a hypothetical; لَا is a simple negation of fact
لَن negates a present action with uncertainty; لَا negates a past action definitively
لَن permanently and definitively negates a future action for all time; لَا is a general negation without that permanence
لَن negates unlikely events; لَا negates events that have already happened
questions.explanation: لَن negates a future action permanently and forever — a decisive divine declaration that the Quran will never be successfully challenged. لَا is a general negation; لَن is stronger and more definitive, and history has confirmed this from the Prophet's ﷺ time until today.

questions.question: According to Mujahid, what are الحجارة in the description of Hellfire's fuel, and why are they especially severe?
options: Stones from the mountains of this world that glow red-hot with heat
Stones engraved with the names of disbelievers, reminding them of their deeds
Stones of sulfur (كِبْرِيت), more foul-smelling and pungent than carrion, adding an olfactory torment beyond heat and flame
Stones of iron heated to extreme temperatures, used to strike the inhabitants of Hellfire
questions.explanation: Per Mujahid, the stones are of sulfur (كِبْرِيت), described as more foul-smelling and more pungent than carrion (جِيفَة). This adds an olfactory dimension to the punishment beyond heat and flame.

questions.question: Why is eternity described as تَمَامُ السَّعَادَة (complete happiness) in the tafseer of the Jannah ayah, rather than simply one more blessing?
options: Because even perfect blessings are incomplete if they can be lost — eternity removes the anxiety of death and loss entirely
Because the food and fruits of Jannah change in flavor every time they are served, ensuring perpetual novelty
Because eternal life in Jannah is the fifth and greatest blessing, ranking above the other four
Because the angels of Jannah continuously recite praises that increase the inhabitants' happiness
questions.explanation: The greatest anxiety of this life is the fear of death and loss. Jannah removes that anxiety entirely by making all its perfect blessings permanent — without eternity, even the finest blessings would remain incomplete happiness.

questions.question: Why is جَنَّاتٍ marked with Kasra as its sign of Nasb, even though it is the Ism of Anna?
options: Because it follows a preposition which always triggers Kasra regardless of grammatical position
Because Anna only takes Fatha when its Ism is a masculine singular noun
Because the rule of Anna is suspended when the Ism is indefinite (Nakirah)
Because جَنَّاتٍ is a Jam' Mu'annath Saalim, and this category always uses Kasra as its Nasb marker
questions.explanation: Jam' Mu'annath Saalim always uses Kasra as its sign of Nasb — this is an exception to the general rule. How Nasb is marked depends on the word's grammatical category, not just its position in the sentence.

questions.question: What is a نِدّ, and what were the mushrikeen doing by making أَنداد for Allah?
options: A witness; they called on created things to testify to their acts of worship
A companion; they sought to draw closer to Allah through created intermediaries
An equal or rival; they set up partners alongside Allah in power and worship — the essence of Shirk
A messenger; they claimed created beings could convey divine authority independently
questions.explanation: A nidd is an equal, rival, or partner. The mushrikeen set up idols and created things as equals to Allah in power and worship, which is the essence of Shirk.

questions.question: Which of the following is cited as a dimension of إِعْجَاز القُرآن in these sessions?
options: Eloquence and rhetoric (بَلَاغَة)
The speed at which the Companions memorized and preserved the Quran
The number of times the Quran has been printed and distributed worldwide
The ease of memorization compared to other scriptures
questions.explanation: Three dimensions cited are eloquence/rhetoric (بَلَاغَة), clarity of expression (بَيَان), and composition/arrangement (نَظْم), along with words, meanings, and legislation (شَرِيعَة).

questions.question: What does الرَّيب mean, and in which ayah does it appear in these sessions?
options: Wonder; it appears in the Jannah ayah describing the purified spouses
Rejection; it appears in the ayah describing the fuel of Hellfire
Doubt or suspicion; it appears in وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا, the opening of the challenge ayah
Certainty; it appears in the opening ayah of Surah Al-Fatiha
questions.explanation: الرَّيب means doubt, suspicion, or confusion. It appears in the challenge ayah: وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا.

questions.question: What does the grammatical term جُمْلَة اعْتِرَاضِيَّة mean, as applied to لَن تَفْعَلُوا?
options: An exclamatory clause expressing divine judgment toward the disbelievers
A conditional clause that introduces a hypothetical scenario
A concluding statement that summarizes the main argument of the ayah
A parenthetical clause inserted within the flow of speech to reinforce a point
questions.explanation: A جُمْلَة اعْتِرَاضِيَّة is a parenthetical clause — a sentence inserted within the main flow of speech to reinforce or emphasize a point, without being the primary statement of the ayah.

questions.question: What is وَقُود, and what two things serve as it in Jahannam?
options: The chains of Hellfire; they are made of fire itself and bind the inhabitants
The guards of Hellfire; they are angels and jinns
The gates of Hellfire; there are seven, each for a different category of wrongdoer
The fuel of fire; the two things are the disbelievers (people) and sulfur stones
questions.explanation: وَقُود is the fuel or substance that kindles and sustains a fire. In Jahannam, the two things that serve as waqud are people (the disbelievers) and stones (specifically sulfur stones per Mujahid).

questions.question: What is the grammatical form of أُعِدَّتْ?
options: Active past tense (Madhi Ma'lum), meaning 'Allah prepared it'
Command form (Amr), root وَعَدَ, meaning 'fulfill your promise'
Present tense (Mudari'), root عَدَّ, meaning 'it is being prepared'
Passive past tense (Madhi Majhul), root أَعَدَّ; the Tā' is added because النَّار (the Fire) is feminine
questions.explanation: أُعِدَّتْ is Madhi Majhul (passive past tense), root أَعَدَّ. The active form is أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ (Allah prepared); the Tā' is added because the subject النَّار is feminine.

questions.question: According to the majority of mufassiroon, what is similar and what is different about the fruits of Jannah described as مُتَشَابِهًا?
options: The shape, color, and appearance are similar, but the taste and quality are different each time they are served
The names are the same but the nutritional benefit is entirely different
The fruits are identical in all respects to fruits of this world, but their spiritual benefit varies
The color differs each time, but the taste is always identical
questions.explanation: According to the majority of mufassiroon, the fruits of Jannah are similar in shape, color, and appearance, but entirely different in taste and quality each time they are served.

questions.question: According to Imam Mujahid, from what specific things are أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَة purified?
options: From physical impurities including Haydh, Nifas, Ghaa'it, Bawl, and Nukhaam
From sadness, anger, jealousy, and fear — all emotional impurities
From the effects of old age, disease, fatigue, and death
From sin, arrogance, envy, and deception — all moral impurities
questions.explanation: Per Imam Mujahid, the wives of Jannah are purified from Haydh (menstruation), Nifas (postpartum bleeding), Ghaa'it (defecation), Bawl (urine), and Nukhaam (sputum/phlegm) — all physical impurities of the human bodily condition.

questions.question: What is the Quranic rhetorical purpose of تَرْغِيب وَتَرْهِيب — placing the description of Jannah immediately after the description of Jahannam?
options: To establish that both destinies were prepared before the creation of humanity
To show the proportional balance of reward and punishment in divine justice
To allow grammarians to contrast the sentence structures used for each destination
To move the heart in both directions — Jannah motivates through hope and Jahannam deters through fear
questions.explanation: Targheeb motivates through hope of Jannah, and Tarheeb deters through fear of Jahannam. Placing them side by side maximizes the simultaneous effect on the reader's heart.

questions.question: How does the restriction on the Quran for a woman in Haydh differ from that of a woman with only Hadas Asghar?
options: A woman in Haydh may recite silently but not aloud; a woman with Hadas Asghar may recite in any manner
Both face identical restrictions — neither may touch the text or recite from memory
A woman in Haydh cannot recite at all nor touch the text; a woman with only Hadas Asghar may recite from memory but not touch the text
A woman with Hadas Asghar cannot recite at all; a woman in Haydh may recite but not touch the text
questions.explanation: Hadas Asghar restricts touching the physical text but permits recitation from memory. Haydh is a Hadas Akbar encompassing the entire body — it prohibits recitation entirely as well as touching the text.

questions.question: Which condition for Masa on Jorabayn do thin professional/office socks most immediately fail?
options: They cannot be worn continuously for 24 hours without needing replacement
Water seeps through them, failing the water impermeability condition
They are not manufactured from natural materials such as wool or cotton
They were not a known item at the time the ruling was established by the fuqaha
questions.explanation: The first condition is water impermeability — wet hands passing over the sock must not cause water to seep through to the foot. Thin professional/office socks fail this condition immediately.

questions.question: How does the time limit for Masa on الجَبَائِر differ from Masa on Jorabayn?
options: Jabair has no time limit — it remains valid for as long as the bandage or cast is medically necessary
Jabair allows 72 hours for all users, whether resident or traveler
Jabair's Masa expires at the next Salah time regardless of medical need
Both have the same limit: 24 hours for a resident and 72 hours for a traveler
questions.explanation: Masa on Jabair has no time limit — it is valid for as long as the bandage/cast is medically necessary. Jorabayn has a fixed limit of 24 hours for a resident and 72 hours for a traveler.

questions.question: According to Imam Abu Hanifa (Ahnaf), what are the minimum and maximum durations of Haydh?
options: Minimum 3 days and 3 nights; maximum 15 days and 15 nights
Minimum 1 day and 1 night; maximum 10 days and 10 nights
Minimum 1 day and 1 night; maximum 15 days and 15 nights
Minimum 3 days and 3 nights; maximum 10 days and 10 nights
questions.explanation: Per Imam Abu Hanifa: minimum 3 days and 3 nights, maximum 10 days and 10 nights, based on a hadith in Dar al-Qutni and Tabrani in which the Prophet ﷺ stated these parameters explicitly.

questions.question: How does the Sharia treat missed Salah and missed Sawm during Haydh?
options: Both missed Salah and missed Sawm must be made up after Haydh ends
Neither missed Salah nor missed Sawm need to be made up after Haydh ends
Missed Salah is permanently dropped with no makeup required; missed Sawm must be made up after Haydh ends
Missed Salah must be made up; missed Sawm is permanently dropped
questions.explanation: Salah is completely Saqit (dropped) — missed prayers during Haydh are permanently forgiven and never made up. Sawm is Haram during Haydh but Qada is required — missed Ramadan days must be made up, as they are far fewer and manageable.

questions.question: What is the Hanafi position on performing multiple prayers with one Tayammum?
options: A new Tayammum is required for each Fard prayer but Sunnah prayers are exempt
Performing multiple prayers with one Tayammum is permissible — Tayammum is a complete Tahara in itself
Tayammum is only valid until the prayer time expires; a new one is needed for the next prayer time
Only two prayers may be performed — one Fard and one Nafl — per Tayammum
questions.explanation: The Ahnaf hold that Tayammum is a complete Tahara in itself, not limited to a specific prayer or time, so multiple prayers with one Tayammum are permissible — contrasting with Imam Shafi'i who requires a new Tayammum for each prayer time.

questions.question: Under which structural modification does الجَوْرَبَيْن become fully equivalent to Khuffayn for Masa purposes?
options: When it reaches above the ankle and is secured with a strap
When it is woven entirely from sheep's wool rather than cotton or synthetic material
When it has been worn continuously for more than 24 hours without removal
When it is Mujallad (entire outer surface wrapped in leather) or Muna'al (leather applied to the sole only)
questions.explanation: Jorab becomes equivalent to Khuffayn when it is Mujallad (entire outer surface wrapped in leather) or Muna'al (leather applied to the sole only) — both structural modifications qualify it fully for Masa.

questions.question: How does the ruling for Masa on الجَبَائِر differ from Masa on Jorabayn regarding prior wudu?
options: Masa on Jabair does not require prior wudu — the bandage may have been applied at any time in any state of purity
Masa on Jabair requires Tayammum to have been performed first, not wudu
Masa on Jabair requires prior Ghusl, not merely wudu
Masa on Jabair requires prior wudu just as Masa on Jorabayn does
questions.explanation: Unlike Jorabayn, Jabair does not require prior wudu. The bandage may have been applied at any time, with or without wudu — because it is a medical necessity and removing it to wash the limb may cause harm.

questions.question: What does سَاقِط mean in the context of Salah during Haydh, and what is its practical implication?
options: The obligation is transferred — a female guardian may perform it on her behalf
The obligation is completely dropped with no makeup required — missed prayers are permanently forgiven
The obligation is delayed — it must be performed later when the woman is in a state of purity
The obligation is reduced — only two rak'ahs are required during the recovery period
questions.explanation: Saqit means the obligation is completely lifted and permanently forgiven. Missed Salah during Haydh is never made up — a woman must not attempt to do so.

questions.question: How does اسْتِحَاضَة differ from الحَيْض in its ruling?
options: Istihada requires Ghusl after each prayer; Haydh requires only one Ghusl at the end
Istihada and Haydh carry identical rulings; both require full suspension of ibadah
Istihada suspends ibadah for up to 15 days; Haydh suspends it for up to 10 days
Istihada does not suspend ibadah — the woman continues to pray, fast, and fulfill all obligations
questions.explanation: Istihada is irregular or abnormal bleeding outside the valid Haydh window. Unlike Haydh, it does not suspend ibadah — the woman continues to pray, fast, and fulfill all obligations normally.

questions.question: What is the Shari' definition of الحَيْض?
options: Any vaginal bleeding, including post-surgical bleeding, that occurs after puberty in a woman
Irregular bleeding that occurs outside the normal window, as defined collectively by the four madhabs
The state of ritual impurity that a woman enters upon experiencing any type of vaginal bleeding
Blood that flows from the womb of a healthy, mature, non-pregnant woman within valid duration parameters
questions.explanation: الحَيْض is blood that flows from the womb of a healthy, mature woman who has reached puberty and is not pregnant, within the valid duration parameters (minimum 3 days, maximum 10 days per Ahnaf).

questions.question: What is the difference between مُجَلَّد and مُنَعَّل?
options: Mujallad qualifies for Masa; Muna'al does not because it lacks full coverage
Mujallad has leather only on the sole; Muna'al has leather covering the entire outer surface
Mujallad has the entire outer surface wrapped in leather; Muna'al has leather applied only to the sole
Mujallad is a type of Khuff; Muna'al is a type of Jorab
questions.explanation: Mujallad means the entire outer surface of the Jorab is wrapped in leather; Muna'al means leather is applied only to the sole. Both qualify for Masa — Muna'al has a hadith in Sunan al-Bayhaqi as its specific evidence.

questions.question: What is رُخْصَة, and what is the correct attitude toward using it?
options: A strict ruling that should only be applied when there is clear Quranic evidence
A temporary exemption that should be avoided once the hardship has passed
A scholarly discretion; only a qualified scholar may decide when it applies to a specific case
A concession granted by Sharia to ease hardship; using it is an act of gratitude (Shukr) to Allah — refusing it out of false piety is not more virtuous
questions.explanation: Rukhsa is a concession or dispensation granted by Sharia to ease hardship. Taking the concession is an act of Shukr to Allah — refusing it out of false piety is not more virtuous and may amount to failing to appreciate what Allah has given.

questions.question: If a person acts on غَالِبَة الظَّنّ (strong conviction that no water exists) for Tayammum and later finds water, what is the Hanafi ruling on their Salah?
options: The ruling depends on how far from the water the person was when they performed Tayammum
The Tayammum is valid but the person must perform Ghusl as a precaution
The Tayammum and Salah remain valid — per Tarfain (Imam Abu Hanifa and Imam Muhammad)
The Tayammum is invalidated and the Salah must be repeated immediately
questions.explanation: If a person had a strong dominant conviction based on clear facts that no water existed, their Tayammum and Salah remain valid even if water is found later — per Imam Abu Hanifa and Imam Muhammad (Tarfain).
